assessments.technical_explanation: The JS-X-Ray shady-link heuristic matched string literals in the TRANSFORM_PREFIXES array (line 27), which contains colon-prefixed token names like 'chars:', 'last:', 'replace:', 'match:'. These resemble protocol-prefixed URLs to the heuristic but are purely string constants used to identify template transform tokens. Review of the entire file confirms zero network primitives: no fetch, XMLHttpRequest, WebSocket, URL construction, or dynamic import. The module is purely synchronous string transformation (trim, upper, lower, regex match, pad, etc.) with no external I/O as confirmed by the @contract annotation (external_io: none, purity: pure). The signal is a false positive from the heuristic misinterpreting colon-terminated string literals as link-like values.
assessments.layman_explanation: The scanner flagged a line that looks like it might contain links, but it is just a list of text-transform token names like 'chars:' and 'last:'. The file performs only string operations with no network calls or external links of any kind.
assessments.developer_action: none

observations.title: Character whitelist effectively prevents code injection into the Function() constructor
observations.technical_explanation: The character whitelist at line 317 ensures that after stripping known function names, only numeric and operator characters survive. Any variable content containing letters or code-like syntax fails this check and the function returns an empty string, preventing code injection through interpolated variables.
observations.layman_explanation: The math evaluator only permits arithmetic characters and a fixed set of math function names, blocking any code injection through template variables.

observations.title: Examples gallery fetches from same-origin bundled files, not external endpoints
observations.technical_explanation: _EXAMPLES_BASE resolves to a relative path within the extension's installation directory via import.meta.url. The fetch targets index.json and example JSON files that are part of the extension's own bundled assets. This is equivalent in trust level to the extension's own source code being loaded. No dynamic or external URL construction is present; filenames come from the fetched index.json, which itself is a local bundled file.
observations.layman_explanation: The example files are loaded from the extension's own directory, the same trust level as the extension code itself, and require explicit user action to import.
